title: Vertebrate Classes
goal: A practitioner can visually assess the Vertebrate Classes scenario using its published diagram convention.

rubric.must: A rooted branching tree visibly shows the stated sister taxa and their clade relationships.
Horizontal branch lengths visibly vary to encode the supplied evolutionary distances.
The named taxa are legible at the tree tips.
The named clade is visibly highlighted distinctly from the rest of the tree.
A visible scale or distance label identifies the evolutionary-distance interpretation.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the phylo/rectangular exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing visibly presents the supplied rooted rectangular phylogram, with varied horizontal branch lengths, five legible tip labels, distinct purple highlighting for the named Amniotes members, and a labeled relative-divergence scale.

items.evidence: Mammalia and Aves visibly share one immediate ancestor; Reptilia and Amphibia share another; those groups and Actinopterygii branch from the root as specified.
Horizontal segments visibly differ in length, including the slightly longer Mammalia than Aves branch, longer Amphibia than Reptilia branch, and long Actinopterygii branch.
Mammalia, Aves, Reptilia, Amphibia, and Actinopterygii are clearly legible and aligned with their respective tips.
Mammalia, Aves, and Reptilia are distinctly marked in purple and grouped by a purple bracket and shaded region labeled Amniotes; Amphibia and Actinopterygii remain unhighlighted.
A visible scale bar is labeled “0.10 relative divergence,” and accompanying text identifies horizontal distance as relative divergence.
